title: Ground Robots Are Arriving on the Front Lines
gist: A Cogs of War podcast blurb saying ground autonomy has lagged air autonomy but the gap is closing, with Ondas Sentinel's Ryan Hartman and Forterra's Scott Philips discussing fielding autonomous ground vehicles, GPS-denied operation, resilient comms and air-ground teaming. Only the topic list is in the text.

insights.claim: Ground autonomy has long lagged autonomy in the air, but the gap is starting to close as autonomous ground vehicles reach combat use.
insights.speaker: Ryan Hartman, Scott Philips, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Ground robotics suppliers such as Forterra and Ondas are positioned as the next unmanned-systems growth segment.

insights.claim: The discussion covers lessons from Ukraine and Gaza, operating without GPS and with resilient communications, and air-ground teaming as key fielding challenges.
insights.speaker: Ryan Hartman, Scott Philips, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Navigation and communications resilience are key differentiators for ground autonomy vendors.

source_meta.author: Ryan Hartman, Scott Philips, and Jonathan Panter
